issues.source_quote: Нехороший человек? - Редиска.
issues.translation_quote: A bad person? - A rat.
issues.justification: 'Редиска' (nasty/bad guy, a mild slang term that is a running gag) is rendered as 'rat', which collides with 'rat' later used for 'сдавать/раскалываться' contexts and loses the comic euphemistic quality; the gag of the glossary lesson is also muddled because 'rat' and 'spill his guts' blur.

issues.source_quote: Хороший человек? Забыл! Фрей-фея, действительно: Фрей-фея.
issues.translation_quote: A good person? I forgot! A good egg, that's right: a good egg.
issues.justification: The source gag is the Docent forgetting the slang 'фрей' (fey/frayer) word; the translation replaces it with an unrelated phrase and removes the forgetting joke's point. Also loses the 'фраер' slang tie-in.

issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк... Я злой и страшный серый волк, я в поросятах знаю толк.
issues.translation_quote: I'm the wicked, fearsome big bad wolf. I know a thing or two about piglets.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the culturally famous Three Little Pigs song reference is flattened; minor loss of rhyme/song feel.

issues.source_quote: Кину не будет. Электричество кончилось.
issues.translation_quote: That's it! Show's over. The power's out.
issues.justification: The well-known Russian cinema-mechanic joke phrase 'Кина не будет' is rendered neutrally, losing the colloquial/comic flavor; acceptable but weak.

issues.source_quote: - А мои? А Ваших подопечных мы сегодня же вернем на место.
issues.translation_quote: - What about my men? We'll return your charges to prison today.
issues.justification: 'Мои' refers to the kindergarten children? In context Troshkin's concern is about his wards; 'my men' and 'charges' is acceptable but 'prison' is added, a mild addition.

issues.source_quote: Чего? - Пасть порву... В угол поставлю!
issues.translation_quote: I'll make you stand in the corner!
issues.justification: Fine; the kindergarten-teacher habit crossing into thief-talk is preserved.

issues.source_quote: Они могут его распилить, переплавить и даже продать за границу.
issues.translation_quote: They could cut it up, melt it down, or even sell it abroad.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Это у нас с ними цацкаются, на поруки берут
issues.translation_quote: We mollycoddle them, release them into people's care
issues.justification: 'На поруки' is a specific Soviet legal practice (release on surety of a collective); the translation is vague and loses the culturally specific reference.

issues.source_quote: Какая зараза хмыренку этому на Хмыря накапала?
issues.translation_quote: Who was the rotten bastard who told that little fellow his dad was in prison?
issues.justification: 'Хмырь' is a nickname for the father (the character 'Slug'); the translation obscures that the boy is Khmyr's son, and 'Хмыренок' (Slug junior) is lost.

issues.source_quote: Я ее того, бритвой по горлу... в колодце она лежит
issues.translation_quote: I took my razor to her throat... She's in the well.
issues.justification: Acceptable; however the preceding 'Хмырь повесился' is rendered 'Slug's hanged himself' (tense/idiom fine).

issues.source_quote: Сколько я зарезал, сколько перерезал, сколько душ я загубил!
issues.translation_quote: How many have I stabbed and slaughtered? How many souls have I destroyed?
issues.justification: The line is a famous parody of a melodramatic prison song/Don Juan-style boast, delivered by a comic character (Troshkin as Nikola of Petersburg); the exaggerated rhythmic parody is flattened into plain prose.

issues.source_quote: Пасть порву... Ну, человек!
issues.translation_quote: Come on, man! Are you deaf?
issues.justification: Minor loss only.

issues.source_quote: Рыбу я ловил. - Какую рыбу? У лодочной станции... В проруби.
issues.translation_quote: - I was fishing. - Fishing for what? By the boat station... In an ice hole.
issues.justification: The Russian clue is an exchange about hiding the helmet in a hole in the ice; the dialogue is okay but 'Толканул шлем?' (Did you fence the helmet) translated 'sell the helmet' loses slang.

issues.source_quote: Во дает! На фронте!
issues.translation_quote: What a story! At the front!
issues.justification: Docent's absurd claim and the sarcasm of 'Во дает' are flattened; also the irony of a man claiming to be a war veteran loses sharpness.

issues.source_quote: Рябого
issues.translation_quote: Pockface
issues.justification: Spelling error ('Pockface' instead of 'Pockmarked/Pockface') and flat; minor.

issues.source_quote: Нехороший ты человек, Косой, злой, как собака.
issues.translation_quote: You're a bad man, Cross-Eye. Mean as a dog.
issues.justification: 'Нехороший человек' is euphemistic understatement used as a running gag; 'bad man' is blunter.

issues.source_quote: Ну ты даешь!
issues.translation_quote: Well, look at you!
issues.justification: Slightly off; 'You're something else!' would fit.

issues.source_quote: Эй, гражданина! Ты туда не ходи, ты сюда ходи, а то снег башка попадет - совсем мертвый будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Hey, citizen! Don't go that way. Go this way. Snow falls on head that way. You end up completely dead!
issues.justification: Good imitation of broken Russian, but 'Snow falls on head' dropped the 'will' flavor; fine.

issues.source_quote: Физкультпривет!
issues.translation_quote: Greetings, sportsmen!
issues.justification: The comic Soviet 'physical-culture greeting' loses its mock-official flavor; inconsistent with other uses.

issues.source_quote: Нары.
issues.translation_quote: Bunk.
issues.justification: Prison plank beds ('нары') carry a prison-specific connotation; 'bunk' is neutral.

issues.source_quote: Он, говорят, Рябого бритвой по горлу - чик и приветик.
issues.translation_quote: They say he went like this across Pockface's throat with a razor.
issues.justification: Awkward; the idiomatic 'чик и приветик' (snip and goodbye) is lost.

issues.source_quote: Против бритвы - пиджак и брюки.
issues.translation_quote: Against the razor, a jacket and trousers.
issues.justification: Unclear in English; the card-game stakes sense (bet) is lost.

issues.source_quote: Ходи лошадью
issues.translation_quote: Move your knight
issues.justification: Chess terminology fine; but 'Fancy a game of chess' for 'Может козла забьем?' mistranslates: 'козла забить' means playing dominoes.

issues.source_quote: Поймают! Как пить дать - застукают.
issues.translation_quote: They'll catch us, sure as anything.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: - Это не смешно, тетя.
issues.translation_quote: That's not funny, lady.
issues.justification: 'Тетя' is fine.

issues.source_quote: Ничего. Вы уж с ним построже. Проездной!
issues.translation_quote: Your pass!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Ухи, ухи, ухи!
issues.translation_quote: My ears! My ears!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Вр оде.
issues.translation_quote: More or less.
issues.justification: Fine.
